topic: Template Class Specialization with Custom Comparator
explanation: In C++, template classes like std::set can accept template parameters that customize their behavior, such as the comparison criterion used for ordering elements. By providing a custom comparator (e.g., std::greater), developers can change the default sorting order or behavior of the container. This feature leverages C++'s template system to create flexible, type-safe, and reusable data structures that adapt to specific requirements at compile time, exemplifying the power of template programming and generic programming idioms in modern C++.
code_example: // Define a set of integers sorted in descending order using std::greater
// Output the elements in descending order
example_explanation: This example demonstrates defining a std::set with a custom comparator std::greater<int>, which sorts the elements in descending order instead of the default ascending order. The set is initialized with some integers, and additional elements are inserted. When iterated over, the elements are printed in descending order, illustrating how template parameters can be used to customize container behavior at compile time, a key feature of template class specialization in modern C++.
